reviewers.method: Read review-rubric.md, form-contracts.md, contracts.json and the exercises.ts cues. Inspected all 14 contact sheets (4 views x 8 phases; 16 phases for the get-up) and enlarged individual frames at the key phases (backswing, top, rack, lockout, bottom, get-up stages). Used geometry.json (no validator failures) and read positions from the exported clip JSON (assets/animations/*.json) for the backswing bell depth, rack/curl bell position and get-up torso height to confirm what I saw. Not observed: real-time playback, timing, easing, loop-seam smoothness or native-size viewing; these are recorded as unrun. Did not refetch external primary sources; technique judgments rely on the stated contracts/cues and standard kettlebell coaching.

kb-swing.summary: Reads clearly as a two-hand hardstyle swing: the bell is hiked behind the heels between the thighs, the hips snap to a tall stance, the bell floats to about chest height on long arms, and the lifter stays tall until the arms reconnect before hinging again. The load reads as swung, not lifted.

defects.issue: The head and neck drop forward and down in the backswing rather than following the spine. This is minor and does not change the lesson.
defects.fix: Keep the neck in line with the torso in the hinge, with the gaze a few metres ahead on the floor.

kb-deadlift.summary: A clear two-hand floor deadlift: the bell sits between the feet, both hands stay on the handle with straight arms, the lifter stands tall and returns the bell to the floor for a reset. It reads as a lift, not a curl.

defects.issue: In the bottom position the bell sits at the toe line, forward of the ankles, with a fairly squat-like knee bend. This slightly contradicts the cue 'bell between the feet, under the hips'.
defects.fix: Set the bell at mid-foot under the hips and shift a little more of the depth into hip flexion (shins more vertical).

goblet-squat.summary: A convincing goblet squat: the bell is held by the horns close to the chest throughout, knees track over the toes (front view), the feet stay flat, depth is comfortable with a reasonably tall chest, and the lifter stands fully.

defects.issue: The torso leans forward noticeably at the bottom and the bell drifts slightly off the sternum. This is within normal variation.
defects.fix: Optionally keep the chest a little more upright at depth so it matches 'keep a tall chest'.

kb-reverse-lunge.summary: A clear alternating goblet reverse lunge: a rearward step, the front foot stays planted (support drift 0), the back knee lowers under the hip with the torso upright, the lifter returns to standing, then switches sides at phase 0.5 with a symmetric second rep.

kb-side-lunge.summary: A clear alternating goblet lateral lunge from a wide stance: the hips sit back over one bent knee while the other leg stays long, feet stay flat, the lifter returns to centre and repeats on the other side. The bell stays at the chest.

defects.issue: The hips sit back only moderately. The shift reads mostly as sideways knee bend.
defects.fix: Optionally add a little more hip hinge at the bottom so it matches 'sit the hips back'.

kb-upright-row.summary: The lift and lower are present, but the top position contradicts the stated variant and cue. The elbows rise well above shoulder height and the bell travels out in front of the chest, not close to the body.

defects.issue: At the top the elbows sit at about ear/head height while the hands are only at the sternum, so the upper arms point upward. The contract says 'elbows below shoulders' and the cue says 'usually below the shoulders'. This teaches an aggressive, impingement-prone end range.
defects.fix: Stop the pull with the elbows at or just below shoulder height and the hands at lower-chest height, with the elbows leading out to the sides.

defects.issue: From the side the bell hangs about 15–20 cm in front of the chest, with the upper arms flexed forward. This reads like a front raise or high pull rather than a close vertical row ('keeping the bell close').
defects.fix: Keep the bell path vertical, a few centimetres from the torso, and drive the elbows up and out to the sides, not forward.

kb-bent-row.summary: It is recognizable as a two-hand bent-over row: a stable hinge, straight arms at the bottom, and a pull with the elbows moving behind the torso. However, the pull ends at the hip crease/belly and the hinge is fairly upright, so it only partly matches 'row toward the lower ribs'.

defects.issue: At the top the bell reaches only the belt line/upper thigh, not the lower ribs. The torso is only about 45° from vertical, which makes the movement read partly as a shrug-curl.
defects.fix: Hinge further (torso closer to 30–45° above horizontal) and pull the bell to the lower ribs, with the elbows driving back past the torso.

defects.issue: The elbows flare laterally rather than travelling back along the ribs.
defects.fix: Keep the elbows closer to the sides as they drive back.

kb-side-bend.summary: The side bend toward the bell in the left hand, with the right hand on the hip, is present and there is no forward lean. However, the bell hangs away from the thigh instead of sliding down it, and the free hand drifts off the hip at the bottom.

defects.issue: The bell hangs several centimetres outboard of the thigh throughout (it does not 'slide down the outer thigh', as the cue and contract say). The right hand lifts off the hip with the elbow flared at maximum bend.
defects.fix: Keep the bell in contact with the outer thigh as it lowers toward the knee, and keep the right palm fixed on the hip through the whole bend.

defects.issue: The range is modest and part of the tilt comes from the head and shoulders.
defects.fix: Show a slightly larger lateral flexion through the trunk, with the head staying in line.

kb-curl.summary: A clear single-arm left curl: the elbow stays pinned beside the ribs (shoulder/elbow depth stays constant), with full flexion and a slow lowering. However, the bell does not hang as a weighted object near the top of the curl.

defects.issue: Near the top the bell ball sits about 14 cm ahead of the wrist and only slightly below it, projecting forward from the hand as if rigid. A handle-held 16 kg bell would hang under the hand or rest against the forearm, so the load stops reading as heavy.
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the ball hangs below the handle (or rests on the forearm in a bottoms-down/horn grip) through the upper half of the curl.

kb-halo.summary: A convincing alternating halo: the bell is upside down by the horns at a front reset, circles close around the head with the elbows raised behind, returns to the front, then reverses direction for the second circle. The torso and feet stay steady.

defects.issue: At the sides the bell passes close to the ear at head level. This is acceptable, but I could not verify how smooth the circle is from 8 stills.
defects.fix: None required. Confirm in playback that the bell path stays circular without stalls.

kb-clean.summary: The hike (the bell goes behind the heels), hip snap and landing in a rack are present, so it is recognizable as a clean. However, the rack is held away from the body and the upswing casts the bell out like a swing, so it does not teach the close elbow-in path or the supported rack.

defects.issue: In the rack the hand is about 20 cm ahead of the shoulder and the elbow is in front of the torso, not tucked to the ribs. The bell projects forward of the hand in side view instead of resting against the forearm and chest. This contradicts 'elbow tucked, bell resting outside the forearm'.
defects.fix: Bring the wrist in to the collarbone/chin line, tuck the elbow onto the ribs or hip crest, and seat the ball against the outside of the forearm and the chest.

defects.issue: After the hip snap the arm is fully extended with the bell about 35 cm forward at hip height, like a swing float, before the pull begins. This teaches casting rather than 'pull the elbow back and in'.
defects.fix: Once the hips extend, bend the elbow early and keep the bell close to the body on a short, vertical path into the rack.

kb-press.summary: A clear single-arm strict press: the lifter starts from the rack, the forearm stays roughly vertical under the bell as it rises, and the lockout is straight with the biceps by the ear and the bell on the back of the forearm, followed by a controlled lowering and no leg drive. The rack start/finish has the same forward-held defect as the clean.

defects.issue: In the rack the bell sits in front of the shoulder with the elbow forward and away from the ribs, rather than seated against the forearm and chest.
defects.fix: Use a tight rack: wrist at the collarbone, elbow on the ribs, bell resting outside the forearm.

defects.issue: The knees stay visibly soft for the whole press. This fits the brace/glute cue less well.
defects.fix: Straighten the knees (glutes locked) during the press.

kb-snatch.summary: A convincing single-arm snatch: the bell is hiked behind the heels, the hips drive, the elbow pulls high with the bell close, the hand punches through, and the lockout is overhead with the bell on the back of the forearm. The drop from lockout is the weak phase.

defects.issue: On the drop the arm swings out to horizontal with the bell resting on top of the hand about 40 cm in front at shoulder height. The bell reads as balanced rather than turning over and falling, so it partly contradicts 'turn the bell over and let it fall'.
defects.fix: Show the bell turning over near the head and falling close to the body into the hinge, rather than arcing out on a straight arm.

kb-getup.summary: The middle of the get-up is good: post on the hand, a high bridge, a straight-leg sweep to a half-kneel with the shin pointing back, an upright half-kneel, a tall split stance with the back toes planted, and a mirrored descent, all with the bell arm vertical. However, the loop never lies down. It starts and ends propped on the right elbow (chest height ≥ about 40 cm in every frame), so the floor start and the roll to the elbow, which are the first cues, are never shown.

defects.issue: Phase 0 is already on the elbow with the torso raised. The contract's first phase 'Lie with the bell pressed; roll onto the planted right elbow' and the counting 'back down' are missing, so the viewer never sees the start or finish position of a rep.
defects.fix: Start and end each loop supine with the bell pressed up over the shoulder and the left knee bent, then show the roll to the right elbow (and the reverse at the end).

defects.issue: During the sweep the torso pitches far forward over the posting hand, nearly horizontal. It reads more like crawling than a controlled hip-hinge sweep, though the knee lands correctly.
defects.fix: Keep the chest more open, facing the bell, as the leg sweeps under the hips.

reviewers.method: Inspected all 14 contact sheets (front, threequarter, left, right rows; 8 phases, 16 for get-up) and enlarged native 480x480 frames for key phases of every exercise; cross-checked geometry.json clearances and read figure.ts, hand-model.ts, kettlebell-model.ts and contracts.json. Could not observe playback: timing, pacing and loop smoothness not directly observed (geometry reports sub-mm loop seams). Views between the four sampled angles and phases between samples were not inspected.

kb-swing.summary: Clearest clip in the set: hinge, hip drive and chest-height float read in every view; the dark bell hangs convincingly below long arms and differentiates it from the deadlift.

defects.issue: Forearms graze the thighs (-5 mm) at the bottom of the backswing; hands and bell merge into one blob between the knees in the front view
defects.fix: Widen the backswing path by ~1 cm so forearms clear the thighs; optional minor

kb-deadlift.summary: Floor start, stand and floor reset are readable and the bell visibly touches the floor between the feet; arm/thigh interpenetration near lockout is the remaining visible defect.

defects.issue: Forearms sink ~2 cm into the thighs as the figure stands (upper arms -1 cm at 0.95); arms and thighs fuse into one silhouette in side views
defects.fix: Move the hang path or shoulders forward slightly so arms rest on, not inside, the thigh surface

defects.issue: At the floor position hands, handle and knees cluster tightly; grip reads only as two white blobs over the handle
defects.fix: Slightly widen stance/knee track or lower camera emphasis so the handle and both hands separate

goblet-squat.summary: Goblet hold at the chest is obvious in all views, depth and upright torso read clearly, and feet stay planted.

defects.issue: Upper arms touch the thighs at depth (-4.5 mm), minor merge of elbow and knee silhouettes
defects.fix: Tuck elbows a few mm inside the knees or reduce depth slightly

kb-reverse-lunge.summary: Step-back, rear-knee drop and alternation are clear in three-quarter and side views; goblet hold stays readable.

defects.issue: The rear leg hides behind the front leg, so the lunge reads as a shallow one-leg squat from the front
defects.fix: Acceptable for a sagittal lunge; optionally angle the stepping line a few degrees so the rear shin shows from the front

kb-side-lunge.summary: Wide stance and weight shift to each side are clear from front and three-quarter; nonworking leg stays long.

defects.issue: From pure side views the lateral shift is invisible and the pose reads as a goblet squat
defects.fix: Inherent to a frontal-plane move; no change required, but default the camera to front/three-quarter for this exercise

kb-upright-row.summary: Bell travels close to the body to chest height with elbows leading; distinct from clean and curl in all views.

defects.issue: At the top the elbows rise above shoulder level and the forearms/hands form a tight cluster over the upper chest, partly obscuring the bell handle
defects.fix: Stop the top a little lower (elbows at or just below shoulder height) so hands and handle stay separate from the shoulders

kb-bent-row.summary: Hinge and two-hand pull read in side and three-quarter views, but the pull amplitude is small and the front view barely changes.

defects.issue: Bell only rises from knee to lower-thigh height; front view frames 0 and 0.5 look nearly identical and the clip is easily confused with a hinge hold/deadlift
defects.fix: Increase row travel so the bell reaches the lower ribs/navel and the elbows clearly pass the torso line

defects.issue: Bell sits ~3 cm from the thigh at the top, visually overlapping it in side view
defects.fix: Draw the bell path slightly further from the thighs as it rises

kb-side-bend.summary: The lateral bend is visible from the front and three-quarter, but the bell does not ride the outer thigh, the free hand leaves the hip, and side views show almost nothing.

defects.issue: Right hand drifts off the hip and floats beside the waist at the deepest bend, breaking the 'hand on hip' cue
defects.fix: Pin the right hand to the iliac crest throughout the bend

defects.issue: Bell hangs 5-10 cm outside the thigh and tilts off plumb, so it neither slides down the outer thigh nor reads as a hanging weight
defects.fix: Keep the bell plumb under the handle and against the outer thigh as it slides down

defects.issue: Side views show only a standing figure with the bell over the thigh; the bend is not legible
defects.fix: Increase bend amplitude slightly and default the camera to front/three-quarter for this exercise

kb-curl.summary: The elbow-flexion arc is visible, but at the top the bell sticks out horizontally in front of the fist, defying gravity, and at the bottom it passes into the thigh.

defects.issue: Bell body is cantilevered forward of the fist with the handle horizontal, at hand height; the weight looks glued on and weightless, and the forearm stops short of full flexion
defects.fix: Hang the bell body below the handle (or rest it against the forearm for a bottoms-down curl) and bring the forearm to full flexion near the shoulder

defects.issue: Bell interpenetrates the front of the thigh by ~2 cm at the bottom
defects.fix: Offset the hang position so the bell clears the thigh by a few mm

kb-halo.summary: The circle around the head reads in three-quarter and side views and the horns grip is plausible, but the front view loses the bell behind the head and the action is small in a full-body frame.

defects.issue: Bell disappears completely behind the head; only raised elbows are visible, so the rear pass is unreadable from the front
defects.fix: Keep the bell slightly lower/offset behind the head so part of the body shows, or apply the contract's upper-body crop so the loop fills the frame

defects.issue: Full-body framing leaves the bell circle occupying a small area at 480 px; hands and horns are hard to resolve
defects.fix: Use the upper-body three-quarter crop the contract specifies

kb-clean.summary: Backswing, hip drive and rack are all present and distinct from swing/snatch, but the rack does not show the bell resting on the forearm and the arm clips the thigh.

defects.issue: In the rack the bell body projects horizontally in front of the fist at chin height instead of resting on the outside of the forearm; it reads as floating
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Upper arm passes ~1 cm into the thigh in the backswing
defects.fix: Keep the working arm on the thigh surface during the hinge

kb-press.summary: Rack-to-lockout path is clear and differentiated, but the bell is drawn lying sideways at both rack and lockout, undermining weight and the 'back of forearm' cue.

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Rack bell sits forward of the fist on a horizontal handle rather than against the forearm
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

kb-snatch.summary: Lockout, drop, backswing and high pull are distinct from the clean and swing, but the lockout bell floats sideways and the bell grazes the thighs in the backswing.

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: Bell intersects the far thigh (-4.6 mm) and the working upper arm the near thigh (-7 mm) in the backswing
defects.fix: Widen the backswing path so bell and arm pass between the thighs

kb-getup.summary: Major stages (post, bridge, sweep, half-kneel, stand) are recognisable in side views, but the loop never shows the supine start, the bell floats sideways overhead throughout, and front/three-quarter transitions tangle.

defects.issue: Loop starts already propped on the hand; there is no lying-down frame, so the start of the get-up is not shown
defects.fix: Include the supine start with the bell pressed and floor contact of back and shoulders

defects.issue: Bell body sits beside the fist at handle height with the handle horizontal, as if the bell were lying on its side in mid-air; it does not rest on the back of the forearm and reads weightless; the bell is the viewer's focus in this exercise
defects.fix: Orient the bell so the handle runs diagonally through the palm and the body hangs below/behind the handle against the back of the forearm (body centre below the handle, axis tilted), keeping the grip ring on the handle

defects.issue: During the bridge and sweep the head drops sideways and the support arm, far leg and torso overlap into an unreadable knot; support-hand contact is hard to see
defects.fix: Adjust the sweep path or the default camera so the posted hand, knee and planted foot separate in silhouette

reviewers.method: Inspected all 14 contact sheets (front, threequarter, left, right) and enlarged individual frames; read geometry.json; probed the motions with python (pose_for, v2.body balance_report, v2.collide) at 120-960 samples per loop using real clip durations (halo 8 s from profiles.json) for knee/elbow angles and flexion-plane direction, trunk lean, COM/ZMP margins, capsule clearances incl. bell-head, bell hang angle relative to the handle, and bell/wrist velocity/acceleration. Could not watch playback at native size: timing, smoothness and loop seams were judged only from sampled kinematics. Reviewed independently without other scores.

kb-swing.summary: Physics-driven pendulum gives a credible hinge, float and free-fall return; the body+bell COM stays over mid-foot (COM margin >=0.119 m, ZMP >=0.109 m) and the bell reads as a 16 kg mass. Remaining issues are small.

defects.issue: Top of the swing shows knees ~22 deg flexed (max knee angle 158 deg), so the hip/knee lockout at the float is soft rather than a tall plank.
defects.fix: Raise pelvis height at h=0 so the knees reach ~170-175 deg at the float.

defects.issue: Forearms overlap the inner-thigh capsules by 5 mm at the bottom of the hike (intended contact, cosmetically acceptable).
defects.fix: Optionally shift BACK_STOP slightly so contact is tangent, not overlapping.

kb-deadlift.summary: Credible floor-to-lockout lift with the bell on a vertical path between the feet, neutral spine and good load-aware balance (COM margin >=0.118 m). The lockout is not a true lockout and the arms are not long.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~30 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 150 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

defects.issue: Elbows are held at a constant 154 deg (26 deg flexion) throughout, so the arms look slightly bent instead of hanging long under a 16 kg load.
defects.fix: Use the full reach (or model the grip at the palm) so elbows are ~170 deg with arms plumb.

defects.issue: Forearm capsules overlap the thighs by 2.0 cm and upper arms by 0.5 cm at lockout (allowlisted contact but visibly pushing into the legs).
defects.fix: Widen the grip lateral offset or narrow the thigh path so the arms rest tangent to the thighs.

goblet-squat.summary: Deep squat is well articulated: knees track the toes, heels down, torso <=30 deg forward, elbows inside the knees, balance margin >=0.09 m. The top position is a partial stand.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~36 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 144 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

defects.issue: Bell overlaps both forearms by 1.3 cm in the goblet hold (allowlisted contact, minor).
defects.fix: Move the bell 1-2 cm forward from the chest or adjust horns height.

kb-reverse-lunge.summary: Good lunge geometry (vertical front shin, rear knee ~3 cm above floor, rear heel lifted, upright trunk) with a pre-step weight shift and pinned feet. Balance during the single-leg step phases is marginal and standing between reps is a crouch.

defects.issue: During single-leg stance the static COM is 0-2 cm outside the stance foot (min -0.020 m at 0.45) and the ZMP only 3-4 cm inside; dynamically valid but the body looks like it is tipping as the rear foot leaves/returns.
defects.fix: Shift the pelvis further over the stance foot before lift-off and hold it until touchdown so the COM margin is >=3 cm.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~36 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 144 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

kb-side-lunge.summary: Lateral weight shift with a planted wide stance: bent knee tracks the toes, trailing leg straight with flat foot, upright trunk, balance margin >=0.10 m. Credible for the represented (non-stepping) variant.

defects.issue: Trunk stays nearly vertical (lean <=24 deg) with the goblet bell; a slight forward hip hinge would better counterbalance the load at depth (minor).
defects.fix: Allow 5-10 deg more forward trunk lean at the bottom.

kb-upright-row.summary: Arm path, elbow-above-hand pull and bell hanging plumb are credible and balance is fine. The whole set is performed in a quarter-squat.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~39 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 141 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

kb-bent-row.summary: Stable 50 deg hinge with fixed pelvis, neutral head/spine, plumb hanging bell, elbows driving back past the torso and clearances >=2.8 cm. Credible reference.

defects.issue: Row top shows elbows only modestly behind the torso line; acceptable, no anatomical defect.
defects.fix: None required.

kb-side-bend.summary: Lateral trunk flexion toward the bell with a pelvis counter-shift reads correctly and balance is good, but posture artifacts remain.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~35 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 145 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

defects.issue: The free (right) hand leaves the hip and floats with the upper arm abducted near horizontal as the trunk tilts, so the 'hand on hip' support is lost.
defects.fix: Pin the free palm to the pelvis/iliac crest in pelvis space so it stays on the hip through the bend.

defects.issue: The spine bends as one rigid block from the pelvis (single trunk segment), so lateral flexion looks like a whole-trunk tilt rather than a lumbar curve.
defects.fix: Distribute bend over a lumbar/thoracic split if the rig allows; otherwise limit the pelvis shift so the tilt reads as spinal.

kb-curl.summary: Elbow stays at the flank and flexion is credible, but the bell does not obey gravity on its handle and the stance is crouched.

defects.issue: At the top the bell centre is held 62-65 deg off plumb from the handle with 3.5 cm clearance to the forearm, i.e. cantilevered in space; this needs ~23 N.m of wrist torque and reads as weightless.
defects.fix: Either let the bell hang plumb from the handle or rest it on the forearm (contact) as in a standard KB curl.

defects.issue: At the bottom the bell is tilted 27 deg off plumb and still overlaps the thigh capsule by 1.8 cm.
defects.fix: Move the hanging hand slightly outward/forward so a plumb bell clears the thigh.

defects.issue: Standing/lockout posture keeps the knees ~39 deg flexed (hip-knee-ankle 141 deg): hips sit ~4 cm below full height because the stance width plus fixed pelvis height leave the legs short of extension, so the lift never visibly finishes tall.
defects.fix: Raise the standing pelvis height per stance (or narrow the ankle offset) so the knee reaches >=170 deg at lockout/standing, keeping heels planted.

kb-halo.summary: Horns-grip orbit is anatomically credible: bottom-up in front, hanging behind the head with elbows raised, arms clear of the head (bell-head >=2.6 cm), steady tall stance and ample balance margin at the 8 s timing.

defects.issue: The legacy (non-v2) motion keeps pelvis and chest perfectly static while 16 kg travels ~0.58 m front-to-back; balance stays valid (COM shift ~2.5 cm) but no subtle counter-lean shows the load.
defects.fix: Optionally run it through the load-aware Lift balance to add a 1-2 cm hip counter-shift.

defects.issue: Palms overlap the bell by 0.9 cm (grip contact, minor).
defects.fix: Tangent-fit the horn grip.

kb-clean.summary: Hinge, backswing between the knees and rack geometry are credible and balance is good, but the bell is spline-driven, so its motion does not show ballistic momentum.

defects.issue: Leaving the rack the bell is driven down at up to 22 m/s^2 (>2 g) for ~0.1 s, so it is yanked down rather than dropped.
defects.fix: Limit the rack-to-backswing descent to <=g (let the bell fall and guide it), e.g. with a pendulum/physics pass like the swing.

defects.issue: After the hip snap the bell slows from ~1.6 to 0.56 m/s at 0.60 (hips already extended) and then re-accelerates to 1.1 m/s, implying an arm curl instead of hip-driven momentum; bell-orientation keys also produce 60+ m/s^2 spikes.
defects.fix: Make hip extension the peak acceleration and let the bell decelerate monotonically into the rack; derive bell tilt from grip acceleration rather than keys.

defects.issue: The arm and bell swing ~40 deg out in front on the ascent, far from the body for a clean.
defects.fix: Keep the elbow closer to the ribs so the bell rises near the body.

kb-press.summary: Rack, wrist-over-elbow path and lockout with the bell on the back of the forearm are credible; balance is fine. The load dynamics are not those of a grind.

defects.issue: The wrist accelerates into lockout (0.58 -> 1.08 m/s at ~0.37) and the bell whips over the wrist (tilt 72 -> 107 -> 92 deg; bell speed 1.9 m/s, 48 m/s^2 up then -21 m/s^2) before settling; a strict press with 16 kg slows near lockout and the bell stays fixed on the forearm.
defects.fix: Use a decelerating (min-jerk) press to lockout and keep the bell's forearm-relative angle fixed during the press.

defects.issue: The same bell flip-over repeats on the descent (tilt 94 -> 112 -> 83 deg).
defects.fix: Hold the bell orientation on the forearm while lowering to the rack.

kb-snatch.summary: Backswing, hip drive, high pull, punch-through wide of the head (bell-head >=14 cm) and overhead lockout are credible with good balance; the bell flip-over on the drop is plausible. Momentum is still authored.

defects.issue: Keyed bell orientation produces vertical bell acceleration spikes up to 77 m/s^2 at the hip drive, larger than the hand motion supports, so the bell appears to snap rather than be thrown.
defects.fix: Drive bell tilt from grip acceleration (as in the swing sim) or smooth the orientation keys.

defects.issue: Upper arm and bell overlap the thigh capsules by 0.2-0.7 cm in the backswing (minor).
defects.fix: Shift the backswing hand 1 cm medially/back.

kb-getup.summary: Strong support logic: bell arm stays exactly vertical throughout, contacts (buttock, elbow, palm, knee, feet) are pinned with zero drift, and COM/ZMP stay inside the support. Some transitions remain questionable.

defects.issue: During the leg sweep back to the bridge the right shin points up/forward while the thigh points down-out; the knee's flexion plane flips relative to the hip axis, requiring >90 deg hip rotation, so the knee briefly reads as bending sideways.
defects.fix: Sweep the leg with the knee leading under the hips (shin trailing behind the knee) so knee flexion stays in the sagittal plane.

defects.issue: Balance margin on the elbow post is only 1.2 cm (COM near the edge of the buttock/elbow/foot polygon).
defects.fix: Shift the trunk slightly toward the posting elbow so the COM sits >=3 cm inside.

defects.issue: Head is rigidly fixed in line with the trunk (neck never rotates), so the gaze cannot track the bell; anatomically possible but stiff.
defects.fix: Add neck rotation/extension to keep eyes on the bell.
